comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: PR description's "Prod-code changes" section describes the fix the strip commit removed**

The PR body (section *"Prod-code changes (exactly two, review-verified)"*, item 2) still states that `_dialAskDeployment` uses `client: modelFetchClient('dial')` — "no-op for unbound providers, **fail-closed proxy routing for bound ones** (closes a wizard-path bypass of the #1921 gate)". The merged HEAD does not do that. Commit `26eb7aecd7` ("scope: strip the wizard proxy-gate fix from the test-perf branch") reverted this call site to a pure test seam:

```dart
deployments = await fetchDialModels(
  baseUrl,
  key,
  client: config.modelsHttpClient,
);
```

In production `AgentCliConfig.modelsHttpClient` is `null` (agent_cli_config.dart:46), so `fetchDialModelsInfo` keeps its own direct `http.Client()` (dial.dart:332, `client ?? http.Client()`) — the wizard-path proxy-gate bypass of #1921 **remains open**, deferred to #249 (as this hunk's own comment says). The code and the strip commit are consistent; only the description is wrong.

Why this matters before merge:

1. The description's reviewer-facing contract claims a prod security-relevant behavior (fail-closed gate) that the diff does not deliver — the ticket body carries the same claim, so future readers of this PR will believe the bypass was closed here.
2. The same section cites "an independent DMTools-method review of the full diff returned APPROVE" — that review covered the pre-strip diff, not this one.
3. The strip is attributed to **#2452** in paragraph 1 but to **#249** in the refs, the commit message, and the code comment — one of the two is wrong.

Suggested fix (no code change needed): update the PR description so "Prod-code changes" item 2 reads `client: config.modelsHttpClient` — pure test seam, production byte-identical, proxy-gate routing for this path tracked in #249 — and reconcile the #2452/#249 references. Everything else in this PR (the seam itself, `fetchDialModels`'s nullable `client`, the MockClient 404 path landing in the same swallowed empty-list branch) was verified correct.

🪶 severity: NIT —
🪶 **NIT: dead test plumbing — `providerNetworks` param + `proxy_connector` import have no remaining consumer**

This PR adds to `cliFor`:

```dart
Map<String, ProviderNetworkConfig>? providerNetworks,
...
providerNetworks: providerNetworks ?? const {},
```

plus `import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/src/providers/proxy_connector.dart';` (line 3) for the `ProviderNetworkConfig` type. These were added for the wizard proxy-binding test (`wizard fetch client: re-run entry name → host → catalog; injection wins`) that the strip commit `26eb7aecd7` then deleted — no call site in this file passes `providerNetworks` anymore (verified by grep: the only occurrences are lines 3, 38, 84).

Remove the parameter, the `providerNetworks: providerNetworks ?? const {}` argument, and the `proxy_connector` import — `dart analyze` stays clean either way, but the leftover implies a provider-network injection seam this file no longer exercises.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
🪶 severity: NIT —
🪶 **NIT: the same future is awaited twice**

```dart
io.sendLine('/exit');
await run;
await run;   // ← duplicate
```

`run` is one `Future` from `cli.run()`; awaiting it a second time completes immediately with the same result, so this is harmless — but it is a reflow artifact (the pre-reflow test ended with a single `await run;`). Drop the second `await run;`.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The test-speed work itself is sound and verified — all six touched suites pass (191 tests, run locally against this HEAD), production behavior is byte-identical (`inboxTickInterval` has exactly one consumer and keeps the 2s default, now pinned by a new test; `modelsHttpClient` is null in prod), and no assertion was weakened — every compressed wait either keeps the same probing power or increases it in tick counts. One important issue: the PR description's "Prod-code changes" section still describes the proxy-gate fix (`modelFetchClient('dial')`, "closes a wizard-path bypass") that commit `26eb7aecd7` stripped — the merged diff ships only the pure test seam and the bypass stays open, deferred to #249.

**Key Issues**:
1. ⚠️ `provider_commands.dart:1910` — stale PR description vs stripped proxy-gate fix (also #2452-vs-#249 inconsistency; the cited APPROVE review covered the pre-strip diff).
2. 🪶 `agent_cli_provider_test.dart:1319` — `OpenRouter auth method picker` group dissolved, its tests now report under `DIAL setup`.
3. 🪶 `agent_cli_provider_test.dart:38` — dead `providerNetworks` param + `proxy_connector` import (only consumer was stripped).
4. 🪶 `agent_cli_viewer_test.dart:921` — duplicate `await run;`.

**Next Steps**:
1. Update the PR description (Prod-code changes item 2) to match HEAD: pure test seam, production null → legacy live client, gate routing tracked in #249; reconcile #2452/#249.
2. Restore the `OpenRouter auth method picker` group boundary; drop the dead `providerNetworks` plumbing and the duplicate `await run;`.

Verified during this review: 191/191 tests green across viewer, provider, inbox_wake, bash_self_defense, release_hygiene, mint; `dart format` clean on all 10 touched files; fixture `--allow-empty` claim holds (no fixture consumer reads the working tree); mint env overrides placed before `...extraEnv` (caller wins); `stillAlive` probe swap keeps identical `ps` semantics with all callers inside POSIX-skip guards.
